newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: PRESS DIGEST-Australian General News - July 15.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-Australian General News - July 15.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

The Reserve Bank of Australia and the Federal Treasury are promoting a review of the primary indicator of inflation and the cost of living, the Consumer Price Index (CPI). These two key agencies want changes in mortgage interest rates to be excluded from the CPI measure, in a move that could have wide-ranging effects. Page 1.

Gloweave, a prominent Australian brand name is to close its last Australian factory, making 85 production staff redundant. The company has a turnover of about A$20 million annually and accounts for 15 per cent Australia's branded business shirt production. With the sale, Gloweave will become an all-imported product. Page 1.

The Reserve Bank of Australia has decided to cease its subsidised cash handling service for the retail banks. The decision is expected to cost businesses and consumers about A$80 million annually, with small and medium-sized merchants set to bear the bulk of the cost increase. Page 1.

Five major Australian environmental groups - Greenpeace, the Australian Conservation Foundation, the Nature Conservation Foundation, the Total Environment Centre and Friends of the Earth - have said they will campaign against the proposed privatisation of electricity in NSW if it contravenes environmental standards. The warning came in a submission to the Hogg committee, which is currently investigating the electricity sell-off. Page 3.
THE AUSTRALIAN

BHP is holding talks with the Indonesian Government on plans to invest in that country's largest steel manufacturer, Krakatau Steel. The news comes on the eve of Prime Minister John Howard's visit to BHP's doomed Newcastle steelworks, where more than 2,00 workers will soon lose their jobs. Page 1.

The most recent Newspoll reveals the Federal Government's lead over the Labor Opposition has fallen from eight points to two during the last month, with its overall primary vote slumping from 44 to 42 per cent. Support for Labor has risen, with its primary vote rising by four percentage points to forty per cent in the same period. Page 1

A detailed survey conducted by respected social researcher Hugh Mackay has revealed Australians are deeply sceptical about Prime Minister John Howard's claims that information technology and small business will provide employment growth. The public has also lost respect for the Prime Minister, and now view him as an ineffective leader. Page 1.

A last minute change in plans led to the death of 12-year-old Katie Bender at the failed demolition of the old Canberra hospital. Katie's family were on their way back from Mass when they stopped at the shores of Lake Burley Griffin where thousands of spectators had gathered to witness the exciting spectacle. Although nearly 500 metres away from the demolition site, Katie died in what police are describing as a freak accident. Page 1.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

ACT officials said yesterday they had not yet received any explanation from the group responsible for the botched demolition of the Royal Canberra Hospital that killed one person. The ACT Government has called for a ban on implosions until the cause of the accident is identified. Page 1.

The NSW Government has given up on attempts to impose a bed tax in exchange for major Sydney hotels agreeing to offer rooms to Sydney Olympics organisers. In another move designed to deflect anger from registered clubs, the Government has agreed to modify plans to increase taxes on poker machines. Page 1.

Katie Bender, the 12-year-old girl who was killed while attending the demolition of the old Canberra hospital, was there only by chance. Her family were returning from Mass and only stopped on the shores of Lake Burley Griffin because they were attracted by the size of the crowd gathered to witness the event. Page 1.

The career of ACT Liberal Chief Minister Kate Carnell is in danger following the botched demolition of the Royal Canberra Hospital. Carnell has had a successful career as a local politician, making her mark as a energetic publicist for the region, but now the odds may have swung against her. Page 1.
THE AGE

The Victorian Government has suggested a national compensation deal for gun dealers, with individual payments of up to A$30,000 being suggested to address income losses since the introduction of stricter firearm laws. A draft proposal is to be put to today's meeting of Australasian police ministers in Adelaide. Page 1.

The death of 12-year-old Katie Bender, who was killed at the public demolition of a Canberra hospital on the weekend, is being mourned by Croatian communities nationwide. The Bender family has received offers of help from the Croatian communities of theACT, Queanbeyan and interstate, and Katie's funeral is expected to be held on Thursday. Page 1.

Over 100 miners are continuing to work at the Hunter Valley No1 coal mine, despite the long-running dispute between management and union there. Each day three buses transporting the workers are escorted by police through a hostile picket line. Page 1.

Australia's ambassador in Cambodia, Tony Kevin, has denied allegations the embassy is refusing asylum to endangered opponents of Cambodian co-Prime Minister Hun Sen. Kevin claims that asylum would be offered in the Australian compound but no one has come forward yet. Page 1.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 937-1800
